thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert - elevated gRPC stream resets from us-west-2a inference fleet. 5m error rate 12% (>3% threshold). Auto-steer to fallback pools triggered (23% of traffic). Escalating to oncall. https://alerts.redwood/INC-33876

alex: oncall here, ack. Seeing increased 502/504s at the NLB layer and grpc stream resets on proxies. No CPU oom spikes yet.

maria: confirming logs from proxy nodes in us-west-2a - lots of ECONNRESET and 'read: connection reset by peer' on downstream streams.
maria: ```
[2026-03-16T22:33:01Z] grpc: stream error code=14 read: connection reset by peer
[2026-03-16T22:33:02Z] tcp close from 10.2.3.45
[2026-03-16T22:34:07Z] epoll_wait returned 0 events
```

samir: checked host metrics - TX queue depth on nic on a subset of hosts is high, packet retransmits up. Looks like intermittent egress plane degradation in AZ. No kernel OOM.

samir: quick mitigation options: 1) reduce NLB connection draining delay, 2) steer more traffic off us-west-2a to us-west-2b/eu-west-1, 3) enable per-customer retry throttling to avoid regen storm.

jordan: we already auto-steered 23%, but sticky sessions to some customers are keeping sessions pinned to affected targets -> increases tail errors. Need to break stickiness for problematic targets.

oncall: agree. Can we set target-group attribute to lower deregistration delay to 10s and reduce stickiness cookie TTL for affected route?

samir: command to set deregistration delay: ```aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn $TG --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=10```

maria: applied on two affected target groups. Starting to see target deregistrations finish faster, new connections should avoid flaky hosts. Monitoring latency now.

jordan: to break sticky sessions for the customer-facing route: set cookie timeout to 30s and add policy to prefer healthy targets. Doing a canary for 5% traffic first.

customer-success: logged 3 customer tickets in the last 12m reporting intermittent 504s for inference calls (tickets #CS-2147, #CS-2148, #CS-2150). One large customer (acct-redwood-42) saw retries spike and token usage doubled. We're drafting a short update.

alex: impact: best-effort - majority traffic sees elevated latency (200-800ms tail) and ~10% 5xx for sessions pinned to bad hosts. Global SLA threshold still intact for most customers due to auto-steer, but a small cohort impacted.

oncall: short-term plan: 1) continue deregs and stickiness TTL reduction (in progress), 2) ramp auto-steer to 40% if errors don't fall in next 10m, 3) deploy routing rule to prefer us-west-2b fallback pools, 4) enable customer-level retry caps for heavy retryers.

samir: I'm enabling retry caps via feature-flag for top 20 noisy customers now. Command: ```curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://controlplane/api/flags/retry_cap -d '{"enabled":true,"limit":3}'```

maria: metrics: since dereg delay change we see target healthy count improving on two TGs and 5xx rate dropping to 6% in the affected route (was 12%). Latency tails still noisy.

jordan: decision: do NOT failover region-wide (would add >150ms median latency). Prefer targeted steer + break stickiness + aggressive drain. If 5xx >8% after ramping steer to 40% then escalate cross-region.

oncall: communications: @customer-success please post status update to impacted customers with ETA ~30-45m and mention mitigations and that we are throttling noisy retries to limit impact.

customer-success: posting update now. Noting affected customers and telling them we mitigated routing, reduced stickiness, and limited retries. Escalated acct-redwood-42 to SE for an immediate call if they request.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout of stickiness TTL change (5% of route) succeeded. No anomalous errors from canary hosts.

samir: preparing a replacement fleet batch - spinning up extra ephemeral proxies in us-west-2b and 2c, will seed cache warmers after they register.

alex: plan for handoff: I'll continue to monitor for 25 more minutes, then hand off to maria for the overnight watch. Maria, you'll own customer comms and escalation if errors rise.
maria: ack, I'll take over at 23:15 UTC. Will keep paging if 5xx > 8% or tail latency > 1s.

oncall: incident timeline note: initial alert 22:32 UTC -> dereg change 22:38 -> canary stickiness 22:47 -> auto-steer to 23% earlier -> further steer to 35% prepped if needed.

alex: adding short postmortem stub to incident page and marking P0 investigation in progress. Handoff to maria at 23:15 UTC. :pager:
